subject: Throughput qualification recap & next steps (Kite Retail pilot)
messages:
From: Elena Petrova <elena@kiteretail.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Mar 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks — quick throughput recap from this morning's call

Rishi / Marissa,

Thanks again for the deep dive this morning. Quick note to capture the things we discussed and a few clarifying questions so we can align on the pilot sizing. High-level summary from our side:

- Primary product flow: real-time price personalization on product detail pages (PDP). Typical request includes 1 prompt + customer profile (avg 450 tokens).
- Expected traffic: baseline steady-state ~80 QPS across global edge (US peak), with intermittent marketing-driven bursts up to ~1,200 QPS for short windows (~2–10 minutes).
- Typical session: streaming responses used to render progressive UI (first tokens should arrive quickly).
- Latency goal: 95th <= 700ms for non-streaming end-to-end, and progressive tokens visible within 200–300ms for streaming UX.

Open clarifying items we need from Redwood to confirm:
1) How you'd map steady vs peak to reserved capacity vs burst?
2) What concurrency assumptions do you make for streaming sessions (KV caching, per-session overhead)?
3) Any guidance on token/sec per GPU for our model family recommendations?

I attached our sample payloads (we'll send a larger dump after lunch). If you can send a short sizing spreadsheet with assumptions, we can validate before Friday.

Thanks,
Elena Petrova
Head of ML Infrastructure
Kite Retail

Attachment: kiteretail_sample_payloads.json (application/json, 42KB)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Elena Petrova <elena@kiteretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Mar 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks — quick throughput recap from this morning's call

Elena — thanks for the clear notes and the sample payload. Below is a concise post-call recap plus the preliminary sizing assumptions we used to build the attached spreadsheet (KiteRetail_throughput_model_v1.xlsx). Please confirm the steady/peak numbers and streaming requirements and we'll lock the pilot BOM.

Post-call recap (our read):
- Workload: PDP personalization, payload ~400–550 tokens (avg 450).
- Traffic profile: steady-state 60–90 QPS (you quoted 80 as typical); short peak windows up to 1,200 QPS (2–10 min), expected ~3–6 peaks/day.
- Concurrency: assume 1.2x requests per active session to account for retries and parallel widget calls (so concurrency ~= QPS * (avg latency in seconds) * 1.2).
- Streaming: progressive partial-render required. We recommend server streaming (chunked tokens) with initial token flush target <= 200ms.
- P95 latency SLO: 700ms (non-streaming); P95 time-to-first-token (streaming) <= 300ms.

Sizing assumptions used in the spreadsheet (summary):
- Model family: quantized 7B-class that matches your quality target (example: open-quant-7b).
- Tokens/sec per GPU (sustained) for this model: 12,000–16,000 tokens/sec depending on batching and sequence length.
- Average tokens per request: 900 tokens (prompt + expected completion budget).
- Effective requests/sec per GPU (steady): tokens/sec per GPU / avg tokens per request => ~13–18 RPS (at 12k–16k tokens/sec).
- To cover steady 80 QPS: pool of ~5–7 GPUs (sustained) depending on batch tuning.
- For short peaks to 1,200 QPS: burst capacity via auto-scale + faster kernels would require ~70–90 GPUs for the burst window (if no extra caching).
- Caching recommendation: prefix and KV caching for repeat users could reduce tokens by 20–40% on PDP lookups — this materially reduces burst GPU needs.

Operational recommendations / next steps:
1) Send us a 24-hour traffic heatmap (15s granularity) and a sample of actual payload sizes — we'll re-run the workbook with real distributions.
2) Confirm whether you can accept model-variant fallback for extreme bursts (smaller quantized model with slightly lower quality) — this is the primary lever to reduce burst capacity.
3) Pilot scope: 2 weeks on dedicated reserved pool sized for steady-state + autoscale to handle 95th percentile bursts for up to 5 mins.

Attached: KiteRetail_throughput_model_v1.xlsx (workbook with conservative and optimistic columns). We flagged assumptions you can edit.

If you'd like, Marissa can run a short tabletop with your infra team to confirm network egress and edge routing for streaming.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

---
Attachment: KiteRetail_throughput_model_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 28KB)
From: Samir Desai <samir.desai@kiteretail.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Petrova <elena@kiteretail.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Mar 2028 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks — quick throughput recap from this morning's call

Rishi — appreciate the detailed breakdown. A few quick clarifications from our infra team after they reviewed the spreadsheet: 

- Our average tokens/request looking at real traffic is closer to 720 (we included fewer completion tokens in the first-pass). Can you re-run the steady-state column with 720 tokens/request?
- For bursts: we do have ~30% of requests hitting the same short user segments where caching would help. Please show an optimistic case (30% cache) vs conservative (5% cache).
- Streaming: we can accept a model-variant fallback for emergency mitigation (smaller model acceptable for <10% of requests during extreme peaks).

We'll drop a larger payload dump into the shared folder by EOD. Also attaching a small sample of real requests for the week (stripped PII).

Samir
Director, Platform Engineering
Kite Retail

Date: Thu, 30 Mar 2028 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks — quick throughput recap from this morning's call

Elena / Samir — great notes and thanks for confirming the caching and fallback tolerance. Quick operational next steps from our side: 

1) Rishi will re-run the workbook with 720 tokens/request and produce two columns: Conservative (5% cache) / Optimistic (30% cache) by EOD tomorrow.
2) We'll put together an MOM and a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) for the pilot (link below) and propose pilot dates (2-week run targeting US region).
3) Monica will kick off a short network pre-check to ensure streaming paths are within the 200–300ms time-to-first-token target — she may reach out for traceroutes.

Proposed owners: Rishi (sizing workbook), Monica (network readiness), Marissa (MAP + pilot coordination).

Look for the updated workbook and MAP tomorrow morning.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
